blocks.heading: Technology changes production
blocks.text: Technology can automate repetitive tasks, improve precision, support design and coordinate inventory or schedules. It can increase acceptable output per input or allow new products, but benefits depend on demand, skills, reliable support and integration. Initial investment, maintenance, energy, downtime and staff development create costs. Some tasks change or disappear while others require new skills. Training may be on-the-job or off-the-job; staff involvement can help implementation. Assess actual productivity and quality after adoption instead of assuming advanced equipment automatically improves performance.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Ota Cutting acquires computer-controlled equipment but staff cannot yet set it accurately. Precision and repeatability are potential benefits, while setup mistakes and downtime can offset them. Suitable instruction and maintenance must accompany the purchase.
